a.xlink:title: Object cloning protocol.
Named integer counters. Counter names can be any nonvar term.
Stream variables (supporting logical, backtracable, adding and retrieving of terms).

Adaptive Boosting classifier using C4.5 decision trees as base learners. Implements the SAMME (Stagewise Additive Modeling using a Multi-class Exponential loss function) variant, which supports multi-class classification. Builds an ensemble of weighted decision trees where each subsequent tree focuses on the examples misclassified by previous trees.
Shared predicates for probabilistic classifiers.

Agglomerative clusterer for continuous datasets. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``clustering_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a clusterer term that can be used for assigning new instances to clusters and exported as predicate clauses.
Shared predicates for clusterer learning defaults, export, and common dataset and encoding helpers.
Portable AMQP 0-9-1 (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) client. Uses the sockets library for TCP communication.
Options processing predicates. Options are represented by compound terms where the functor is the option name.
AMQP connection pool category. Import this category into an object to create a named connection pool with automatic connection management.
Protocol for machine learning anomaly detectors.
Shared predicates for anomaly detector learning defaults, threshold-based prediction, baseline training-data selection, dataset helpers, and export.
Protocol for datasets used with anomaly-detection algorithms.

Protocol for ant colony optimization problem definitions. A problem object must define the required predicates for constructive solution building on a construction graph (typically a complete graph over a set of nodes, as in the TSP). Optional predicates allow custom stopping and progress reporting.

Ant Colony Optimization (Ant System) metaheuristic. Parameterized by a problem object implementing the ``ant_colony_problem_protocol`` protocol and by a random number generator algorithm for the ``fast_random`` library. The algorithm minimizes the solution cost defined by the problem. Classic Ant System pheromone update, optional MAX-MIN pheromone bounds, candidate construction by probabilistic state transition, optional elitist reinforcement, progress reporting, and seed control are supported; suitable defaults are used otherwise.
Ant colony optimization algorithm using the Xoshiro128++ random number generator via ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)``.
Application metadata predicates, including optional source provenance facts.
Application metadata and provenance predicates.
Apriori frequent itemset miner for transaction datasets using deterministic level-wise candidate generation and anti-monotone pruning.
Shared predicates for frequent itemset miner dataset validation, support accumulation, and itemset ordering/filtering helpers.
Adds predicates for generating and shrinking random values for selected types to the library ``type`` object. User extensible.
Type checking predicates. User extensible. New types can be defined by adding clauses for the ``type/1`` and ``check/2`` multifile predicates.
Protocol for arrangements operations over lists.
Implementation of arrangements operations with repetition over lists.
Protocol for process-backed ASP solving, source generation, and result inspection.
Protocol for ordered, ground ASP statement providers.
Canonical ASP statement validation and source generation.
Parser for shown Clingo ground symbols.
Whole-document Clingo and Zetesis JSON output decoding.
Opt-in equivalent ASP directive and clause expansion for pure problem objects.
Isolated operating-system shell transport for ASP solver CLIs.
Process-backed Clingo and Zetesis CLI solving, ASP source generation, and collected result inspection.
Assignable variables (supporting backtracable assignment of non-variable terms) protocol.
Assignable variables (supporting backtracable assignment of non-variable terms).
Protocol for association rule miners deriving scored rules from mined frequent patterns.
Shared predicates for association rule miner diagnostics, options, validation, and export.
Association rule miner deriving confidence- and lift-scored rules from frequent itemsets and sequential patterns.
Protocol for the opaque environment representation used by the ATMS library.
Portable, functional Assumption-based Truth Maintenance System API.
ATMS environments represented as canonical ordered lists of node identifiers.
ATMS environments represented by non-negative integer bitsets. Best suited to a modest number of assumptions.
ATMS environments represented as sparse ordered lists of nonempty 16-bit blocks.
Portable incremental Assumption-based Truth Maintenance System.
Apache Avro binary format parser and generator.
Base32 encoder and decoder (RFC 4648).
Base58 encoder and decoder (Bitcoin alphabet variant).
Base64 parser and generator.
Base64URL parser and generator.
Base64URL parser and generator without padding.
Base85 encoder and decoder (Ascii85/btoa variant).
Naive, seasonal naive, mean, and drift time series forecasters with missing observations and immutable online updates.
Shared predicates for forecaster diagnostics, dataset validation, differencing, lag construction, error metrics, seasonal adjustment, and baselines.

Bayesian ridge regression regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using evidence maximization and posterior uncertainty over coefficients. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``regression_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a regressor term that can be used for prediction, predictive-distribution queries, and export as predicate clauses.
Shared predicates for regressor learning defaults, diagnostics, validation, dataset validation, export, and pretty-print helpers.
Protocol for one-shot encryption and decryption using a block cipher.
Protocol for block ciphers supporting opaque prepared keys for repeated block operations.
AES block cipher implementation shared by the AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 objects.
AES-128 block cipher.
AES-192 block cipher.
AES-256 block cipher.
Shared validation, block, XOR, and PKCS#7 predicates for block cipher modes.
Generic Electronic Codebook mode encryption and decryption.
Generic Cipher Block Chaining mode encryption and decryption.
Generic Counter mode encryption and decryption using a whole-block big-endian counter.
Content-based recommender using raw-count query profiles and Okapi BM25 relevance scores.
Shared collection and validation of item catalogs and content descriptors.
Shared predicates for recommender diagnostics, rating dataset validation, rating-matrix utilities, similarity metrics, and top-k retrieval.

Borda grouped-ranking ranker. Learns one deterministic score per item from a dataset object implementing the ``ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by summing per-group Borda points and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Shared predicates for collecting, analyzing, and validating ranking datasets.
Shared predicates for score-ranker term construction, validation, ranking, export, and pretty-printing.

Bradley-Terry pairwise preference ranker. Learns one positive strength parameter per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol when the directed win graph admits a finite Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood estimate, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Shared predicates for score-based rankers that order candidates using precomputed item scores.
Shared preprocessing, connectivity, and MM-iteration helpers for pairwise strength rankers.
BSON format exporter and importer.
BSON format exporter and importer using atoms for decoded strings and keys.
Predicates for converting between integers and fixed-size byte lists in big-endian and little-endian order.

C4.5 decision tree learning algorithm. Builds a decision tree from a dataset object implementing the ``dataset_protocol`` protocol and provides predicates for exporting the learned tree as a list of predicate clauses or to a file. Supports both discrete and continuous attributes, handles missing values, and supports tree pruning.
Shared predicates for classifier diagnostics, dataset validation, mixed-feature distance calculations, and export.
Protocol for Cartesian-product operations over lists.
Implementation of Cartesian-product operations over lists.
Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) format exporter and importer.
Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) format exporter and importer. Uses atoms to represent decoded CBOR strings.
Character set protocol for converting between lists of character codes and lists of bytes.
US-ASCII character set encoder and decoder.
Single-byte character set implementation parameterized by the maximum valid code.
Shared implementation support category for character set objects.
Single-byte character set implementation parameterized by sparse byte-to-code mapping facts and undefined bytes.
UTF-8 character set implementation.
UTF-8 character set encoder and decoder.
UTF-16 little-endian character set encoder and decoder.
UTF-16 character set implementation parameterized by byte order.
UTF-16 big-endian character set encoder and decoder.
UTF-32 little-endian character set encoder and decoder.
UTF-32 character set implementation parameterized by byte order.
UTF-32 big-endian character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-1 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-2 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-3 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-4 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-9 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-10 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-13 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-14 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-15 character set encoder and decoder.
ISO-8859-16 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1250 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1251 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1253 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1254 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1257 character set encoder and decoder.
Windows-1252 character set encoder and decoder.
Selects categorical or discretized continuous features using Pearson or Yates chi-square, or uncorrected or bias-corrected Cramer V.
Typed preparation of categorical columns with per-feature or joint complete-case discretization.
Shared learning, validation, selection, and export implementations for univariate feature selectors.
Protocol for datasets used with classifier algorithms.
Protocol for machine learning classifiers.
Protocol for classifiers that can estimate class probabilities.
Closed sequential pattern miner for sequence datasets using closure-aware projected-database search.
Shared predicates for sequential pattern miner dataset validation, support counting, and pattern ordering helpers.
Protocol for machine learning clusterers.
Protocol for datasets used with clustering algorithms.
Shared helpers for adaptive search-index construction and range queries used by clustering libraries.
Protocol for one-shot CMAC digest computation using block cipher objects implementing ``block_cipher_prepared_key_protocol``.
CMAC (Cipher-based Message Authentication Code) implementation as specified in NIST SP 800-38B.
Protocol for combinations operations over lists.
Implementation of combinations operations over lists.
Category for defining command-line options. Import this category into objects that represent individual command-line options and override the predicates as needed.
Command line options parsing predicates. Uses object-based option specifications with the ``command_line_option`` category.

Colley pairwise preference ranker. Learns one deterministic rating per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by solving the Colley linear system built from aggregated pairwise outcomes and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.

Extends ``local_optimization_problem_protocol`` with general equality and inequality constraints. Box constraints continue to be expressed via the inherited ``position_bounds/1``. A problem that defines neither ``equality_constraints/2`` nor ``inequality_constraints/2`` is a plain ``local_optimization_problem_protocol`` problem and can still be solved by any ``constrained_optimization`` solver.

Protocol for continuous local-optimization problem definitions. A problem object must define the required predicates and may optionally define gradient, Hessian, bounds, stopping, and progress predicates. The same problem object can be used by any solver in the local_optimization library and by the existing global metaheuristics (PSO, DE, ...).

Protocol for solvers of convex quadratic programs in standard form: minimize 0.5*x^T*H*x + c^T*x subject to Aeq*x = beq and Aineq*x =< bineq. This is a numerical subroutine protocol, not a local_optimization_problem_protocol/constrained_optimization_problem_protocol solver: it operates on plain matrices and vectors, not on problem objects, since it is meant to be called once per outer/SQP iteration on a freshly linearized subproblem.
Shared numeric, objective-direction, and validation predicates for constrained optimization solvers and their internal problem wrappers.
Dense active-set solver for convex quadratic programs. Intended as a subroutine for sqp_active_set(_); also usable standalone for small dense QPs.

Sequential Quadratic Programming local optimizer for problems with general equality and inequality constraints. Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``; constraint predicates and their Jacobians are optional.

Common code for local-optimization solvers: option handling, objective-direction helpers, bound projection, vector utilities, progress reporting, and basic validation. Concrete solvers import this category and implement the search loop.
Augmented Lagrangian method for problems with general equality and inequality constraints, delegating each penalized subproblem to an existing local optimization solver.

Internal augmented-Lagrangian penalized subproblem: objective(x) = Sign*f(x) + penalty(x), where penalty adds the Hestenes-Powell term for each equality constraint and the smooth Rockafellar/Bertsekas term for each inequality constraint at the current multiplier estimates EqLambda/IneqLambda and penalty parameter Rho. Instantiated fresh by augmented_lagrangian(_,_) every outer iteration, starting from StartPoint (the previous outer iterate, not Problem's own initial_point/1, so each inner solve warm-starts from where the outer loop left off); not meant to be used directly.
Quadratic penalty method for problems with general equality and inequality constraints, delegating each penalized subproblem to an existing local optimization solver.

Internal quadratic-penalty subproblem: objective(x) = Sign*f(x) + (rho/2)*(||g(x)||^2 + ||max(0,h(x))||^2). Instantiated fresh by quadratic_penalty(_,_) every outer iteration, starting from StartPoint (the previous outer iterate, so each inner solve warm-starts from where the outer loop left off); not meant to be used directly.
Interior-point log-barrier method for inequality constraints, optionally combined with a quadratic penalty for equality constraints.

Internal log-barrier subproblem: objective(x) = Sign*f(x) - mu*sum_j log(-h_j(x)) + (rho/2)*||g(x)||^2, with the barrier term replaced, per inequality constraint, by a smooth large-coefficient quadratic penalty whenever that constraint is not comfortably strictly satisfied. Instantiated fresh by log_barrier(_,_) every outer iteration, starting from StartPoint (the previous outer iterate); not meant to be used directly.

Internal phase-1 feasibility subproblem for log_barrier(_,_): minimizes sum_j max(0, h_j(x) + margin)^2 (margin = 1.0e-6), an ordinary smooth, everywhere-defined unconstrained objective, so a minimizer that reaches (near) zero gives a point with every h_j(x) < -margin, comfortably inside the barrier's domain rather than exactly on its boundary. Instantiated once, when initial_point/1 is not already strictly feasible; not meant to be used directly. See log_barrier(_,_)'s "ensure_strictly_feasible/3" for how the result is validated and how this heuristic falls back to raising domain_error/2 when it does not succeed.
Infeasible-start primal-dual interior-point method with Mehrotra predictor-corrector for general equality, inequality, and box constraints.

Copeland pairwise preference ranker. Learns one deterministic score per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by comparing aggregated head-to-head outcomes for each observed matchup and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Coroutining predicates.
Parser and generator for user and system crontab files.
Parser and generator for user and system crontab files using atoms for text representation.
Coordinate reference systems and coordinate transformation predicates protocol.

Coordinate reference systems and common transformations for 2D and 3D WGS84 geodetic coordinates, Web Mercator, World Mercator, ECEF, local ENU tangent-plane, Lambert azimuthal equal-area, and UTM coordinates.
Transport-neutral cryptographic helper predicates.

XChaCha20 stream cipher and XChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption with associated data algorithm implementation. Requires exact, unbounded integer arithmetic for the Poly1305 130-bit accumulator.
Ed25519 (RFC 8032) public-key signature implementation. Requires exact, unbounded integer arithmetic for arithmetic modulo the 255-bit field prime and modulo the group order.
X25519 Diffie-Hellman key agreement implementation (RFC 7748). Requires exact, unbounded integer arithmetic for arithmetic modulo the 255-bit field prime.
Identity-authenticated ephemeral X25519 channels with directional XChaCha20-Poly1305 keys, strict counters, and per-message symmetric key ratcheting.
CCSDS transfer frame parser and generator protocol.
Helpers for introspecting CCSDS transfer frame terms.
CCSDS telemetry transfer frame parser and generator.
CCSDS telecommand transfer frame parser and generator.
CCSDS advanced orbiting systems transfer frame parser and generator.
Type definitions for CCSDS transfer frames.
Ergonomic wrappers around the CCSDS TM, TC, and AOS frame objects using explicit profile terms.
Helpers for CCSDS packet service packet-zone splitting and cross-frame TM/AOS packet reassembly.
Helpers for packetizing CCSDS space packets into TM and AOS service-data regions with cross-frame carryover and idle fill generation.
CCSDS Space Packet parser following the CCSDS 133.0-B-2 standard. Parses binary packet data including optional secondary headers.
CCSDS Space Packet parser with no secondary header parsing. For secondary header support, use ccsds_packets(Length) where Length is the secondary header size in bytes.
Type definitions and arbitrary generators for CCSDS packets.
Helpers for CCSDS telecommand segment extraction, insertion, and cross-frame TC service reassembly.
CCSDS time code parser and generator protocol.
Helpers for introspecting CCSDS time code terms.
CCSDS unsegmented time code parser and generator.
CCSDS day segmented time code parser and generator.
CCSDS calendar segmented time code parser and generator.
Type definitions and arbitrary generators for CCSDS time codes.
Helpers for parsing and generating self-describing CCSDS time fields using descriptor terms and the existing CCSDS time-code objects.
Support for asking questions when guessing the separator and the record arity of CSV files.
CSV file and stream reading and writing protocol.
CSV file and stream reading and writing predicates.
Backward-compatible parametric object equivalent to using ``csv(_Header_, _Separator_, _IgnoreQuotes_, false)``.
CSV files reading and writing predicates using the options Header - ``keep``, Separator - ``comma``, and IgnoreQuotes - ``false``.
Cuid2 generator protocol.
Cuid2 generator.
Cuid2 generator using atom representation, 24 symbols, and a lowercase alphanumeric alphabet.

CUSUM (Cumulative Sum Control Chart) anomaly detector for continuous sequence-like datasets. Learns per-step population mean and standard deviation from baseline training examples, or from the baseline subset of a labeled dataset selected by learn-time class-label options, using a dataset object implementing the ``anomaly_dataset_protocol`` protocol. Returns a detector term that can be used for scoring, prediction, and export.
Datalog and incremental rule engine protocol (stratified negation subset).
Portable Datalog engine with stratified negation and incremental updates.
Date protocol.
Date predicates.
Time protocol.
Time predicates.
Protocol for zone-aware date-time conversion using cached TZif data.
Zone-aware date-time conversion bridging the ``dates`` and ``tzif`` libraries.

DBSCAN clusterer for continuous datasets. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``clustering_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a clusterer term that can be used for assigning new instances to clusters and exported as predicate clauses.
Smalltalk dependent protocol.
Smalltalk dependent handling predicates.
Extracted protocol entity.
Double-ended queue (deque) implementation using difference lists to provide O(1) operations at both ends.
Compound data type.
Protocol for derangement operations over lists.
Implementation of derangement operations over lists.
Dictionary protocol.
AVL tree implementation of the dictionary protocol. Uses standard order to compare keys.
Term utility predicates.
Simple binary tree implementation of the dictionary protocol. Uses standard order to compare keys.
Red-Black tree implementation of the dictionary protocol. Uses standard order to compare keys.

Splay tree implementation of the dictionary protocol. A splay tree is a self-adjusting binary search tree with the property that recently accessed elements are quick to access again. Uses standard order to compare keys.
2-3 tree implementation.
Provides dif/2 and derived predicates.
Differential Evolution (DE/rand/1/bin, DE/rand/1/exp, DE/best/1/bin, and DE/current-to-best/1/bin) metaheuristic for continuous bounded optimization.
Differential Evolution using the Xoshiro128++ random number generator via ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)``.
Protocol for continuous bounded Differential Evolution problem definitions.
Protocol for machine learning dimension reducers.
Shared predicates for dimension reducer learning defaults, dataset helpers, transformation, export, and printing.
Protocol for datasets used with unsupervised dimension reduction algorithms.
Protocol for labeled datasets used with supervised dimension reduction algorithms such as LDA.
Protocol for target-valued datasets used with supervised dimension reduction algorithms such as PLS projections.
Eclat frequent itemset miner for transaction datasets using portable vertical tidsets and depth-first recursive prefix extension.
Multiple hidden parameters: an extension to Prolog's DCG notation. Ported to Logtalk as a hook object.

Elastic net regression regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using coordinate descent with coefficient-wise L1 shrinkage plus L2 stabilization. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``regression_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a regressor term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.

Elo pairwise preference ranker. Learns one deterministic rating per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by replaying the observed preference stream using a deterministic batch Elo update rule, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.

e-Means clusterer for continuous datasets. Defaults to the published EMA training algorithm with count-weighted donor splitting and last-epoch-mean finalization. Also supports slow-EMA finalization and a hybrid of EMA training and bounded Lloyd refinement. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``clustering_dataset_protocol`` protocol.
Convenience object for ``emeans_clusterer/1`` using the ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)`` random number generator.
Event registry protocol.
Before and after events registry predicates.
Before events registry predicates.
After events registry predicates.
Monitor protocol.
Monitor predicates.

EWMA (Exponentially Weighted Moving Average) anomaly detector for continuous sequence-like datasets. Learns per-step population mean and standard deviation from baseline training examples selected from a dataset object implementing the ``anomaly_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a detector term that can be used for scoring, prediction, and export.
Hook object for expanding library alias paths in ``logtalk_library_path/2`` facts when compiling a source file.

Constructors for expected terms. An expected term contains either a value or an error. Expected terms should be regarded as opaque terms and always used with the ``expected/1`` object by passing the expected term as a parameter.
Expected term predicates. Requires passing an expected term (constructed using the ``expected`` object predicates) as a parameter.
Types and predicates for extended type-checking and handling of expected terms.
Shared fitting and forecasting predicates for exponential smoothing models.

Bounded sum-of-squared-errors optimization problem for exponential smoothing parameters. Implements both the local-optimization (Nelder-Mead) and Differential Evolution problem protocols over the same objective.
Simple, Holt linear-trend, and additive or multiplicative Holt-Winters exponential smoothing forecaster.

Protocol for datasets used with feature selection algorithms. Generalizes classification_protocols::dataset_protocol to also support regression targets and unsupervised use (no target at all), reusing the same attribute_values/2 predicate for familiarity.
Protocol for pluggable feature scoring criteria used by filter-based feature selection.
Shared arithmetic, discretization, and sparse contingency helpers for feature scoring.
Mutual information redundancy in bits between aligned, already prepared categorical feature columns.

Unsupervised feature scoring by population variance: ignores Targets entirely. A near-constant feature (one that takes almost the same value in every example) carries little information for distinguishing examples and so scores low; this is the classic "variance threshold" filter criterion. Scores 0.0 when every value is missing.

Scores a numeric feature against a numeric target using squared Pearson correlation over complete examples. Returns a score in [0.0, 1.0], independent of correlation sign. Returns 0.0 for fewer than two complete examples or an exactly constant feature or target.

Scores a numeric feature against a categorical target using the one-way ANOVA F-statistic over complete examples, capped at 1.0e10. Returns 0.0 for fewer than two classes, no within-class degrees of freedom, or a constant feature. Perfect class separation scores 1.0e10 and ties with any finite statistic reaching the cap.
Scores a numeric feature against categorical targets using between-class scatter divided by within-class scatter, capped at 1.0e10.
Scores a categorical or explicitly discretized numeric feature against categorical targets using empirical mutual information in bits.
Scores categorical feature values against categorical targets using empirical mutual information in bits. Numeric values are treated as category labels.
Scores a categorical or explicitly discretized numeric feature against categorical targets using the Pearson contingency-table chi-square statistic, without correction or normalization.
Scores categorical feature values against categorical targets using the Pearson contingency-table chi-square statistic. Numeric values are treated as category labels.
Scores categorical features using Yates-corrected chi-square for occupied two-by-two tables and Pearson chi-square otherwise.
Scores a categorical or explicitly discretized numeric feature against categorical targets using symmetrical uncertainty in [0.0, 1.0].
Scores categorical feature values against categorical targets using symmetrical uncertainty in [0.0, 1.0]. Numeric values are treated as category labels.
Scores a categorical or explicitly discretized numeric feature against categorical targets using uncorrected Cramer's V in [0.0, 1.0].
Scores categorical feature values against categorical targets using uncorrected Cramer's V in [0.0, 1.0]. Numeric values are treated as category labels.
Scores categorical or explicitly discretized numeric features using bias-corrected Cramer's V in [0.0, 1.0]. Degenerate tables and nonpositive corrected dimensions score zero.
Scores categorical feature values using bias-corrected Cramer's V in [0.0, 1.0]. Numeric inputs are category labels; nonpositive corrected dimensions score zero.
Protocol for feature selection models.
Shared predicates for selector diagnostics, dataset validation, feature-matrix utilities, and selection strategies (top-k and threshold).
Shared joint nearest-neighbor feature selection for Relief, ReliefF, and RReliefF.
Selects continuous features for categorical targets using Fisher scores, top-k selection, or a score threshold.

Protocol for flow network construction and inspection. A flow network is a directed graph where each arc has a non-negative integer lower bound and capacity, with the lower bound not exceeding the capacity, and an integer cost.

Flow network construction and inspection. The network is an opaque term. Each input arc is stored as a residual pair of arcs: a forward arc with identifier ``2*I`` and a reverse arc with identifier ``2*I+1`` (``I`` being the zero-based position of the arc in the input list), where the reverse arc has zero initial residual capacity and the negated cost. The parametric object parameter is the dictionary object used for the representation and must be the same one used by the flow algorithm objects.
Flow network construction and inspection using the ``avltree`` dictionary.

Support predicates shared by the flow algorithm objects: terminal validation, residual graph traversal, path augmentation, and flow extraction. The category parameter is the dictionary object and must be the same one used to construct the flow network.
Maximum flow and minimum cut protocol.
Maximum flow and minimum cut predicates shared by the maximum flow algorithm objects. Importing objects must define the ``maximize/5`` predicate.

Edmonds-Karp maximum flow algorithm (Ford-Fulkerson using shortest augmenting paths found by breadth-first search). Runs in O(V*E^2) time. Mainly intended as a simple reference implementation; see the ``dinic`` object for a faster alternative.
Edmonds-Karp maximum flow algorithm using the ``avltree`` dictionary.

Dinic maximum flow algorithm. Each phase builds a level graph using breadth-first search and then computes a blocking flow using depth-first search. Runs in O(V^2*E) time. A vertex whose depth-first search fails to push the requested amount is recorded as dead for the rest of the phase, which plays the role of the current-arc pointers of imperative implementations.
Dinic maximum flow algorithm using the ``avltree`` dictionary.

Capacity-scaling augmenting paths. Each phase traverses residual arcs with capacity at least a power-of-two threshold. The standard bound is O(E^2*log(U)), before dictionary costs. This is an alternative to Dinic, not a guaranteed speedup.
Capacity-scaling maximum flow using the ``avltree`` dictionary.
Gomory-Hu cut trees for networks with symmetric aggregate capacities. Uses n-1 calls to Dinic for n vertices, with no calls for empty networks. Costs and self-loops do not affect cuts.
Gomory-Hu cut trees using the ``avltree`` dictionary.
Builds finite, discrete-time flow networks from explicit departure and storage schedules. Expanded vertices are tagged ``time(Vertex, Time)`` terms; schedule arcs retain input order and arc IDs.
Builds time-expanded flow networks using the ``avltree`` dictionary.
Minimum cost flow protocol.

Minimum cost flow using the successive shortest paths algorithm with node potentials (reduced costs), where each shortest path is found using Dijkstra algorithm and a binary heap. Arcs with negative cost are saturated beforehand so that all residual costs are non-negative, which also handles negative cost cycles. Supplies and demands are routed from a super source to a super sink. Integer capacities and costs only.
Minimum cost flow using the successive shortest paths algorithm and the ``avltree`` dictionary.

Builds ordinary flow networks that model convex piecewise-linear integer arc costs by expanding each cost segment into a linear-cost arc. The returned mapping is opaque and records the public vertices and arcs of the expanded network.
Convex piecewise-linear integer cost network builder using the ``avltree`` dictionary.
Formatted output predicates.
FP-growth frequent itemset miner for transaction datasets using recursive conditional pattern-base projection over an FP-tree with header-table and parent-link navigation.
Protocol for transaction datasets used with frequent itemset mining algorithms. Transaction identifiers are expected to be unique within a dataset.
Shared predicates for pattern miner diagnostics, defaults, option handling, and export helpers.

Gaussian mixture model clusterer for continuous datasets. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``clustering_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a clusterer term that can be used for assigning new instances to clusters and exported as predicate clauses.

Gaussian process regression regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using an exact mixed Gaussian process with posterior uncertainty estimates. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``regression_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a regressor term that can be used for prediction, predictive-distribution queries, and export as predicate clauses.

Protocol for genetic algorithm problem definitions. A problem object must define the required predicates for individuals, fitness (energy), crossover, and mutation, and may optionally define initial population generation, stopping, progress reporting, diversity, and adaptive rate hooks.

Genetic algorithm meta-heuristic optimizer. Parameterized by a problem object implementing the ``genetic_algorithm_problem_protocol`` protocol and by a random number generator algorithm for the ``fast_random`` library. The algorithm minimizes the energy (cost) function defined by the problem by default; maximization is supported via options. Custom stop conditions, diversity measures, progress reporting, and selection pressure can be defined by the problem object or configured via options; suitable defaults are used otherwise.
Genetic algorithm meta-heuristic optimizer using the Xoshiro128++ random number generator via ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)``.
Predicates for generating increasing non-negative integers. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
Global object for generating increasing non-negative integers for named counters. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.

Predicates for generating unique atoms. Protocol based on the ``gensym`` module of SWI-Prolog. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
Global object for generating unique atoms. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
GeoJSON (RFC 7946) parser, generator, and validator protocol.
GeoJSON (RFC 7946) parser, generator, and validator built on top of the ``json`` library.
GeoJSON parser, generator, and validator using default JSON term representations.
Geohash predicates protocol.
Geohash encoder, decoder, adjacency, covering, hierarchy, integer conversion, bit-precision, and geometry covering predicates for ``geographic(Latitude,Longitude)`` coordinates.
Geospatial predicates protocol.
Geospatial predicates over geographic coordinates represented as ``geographic(Latitude,Longitude)``.
Predicates for accessing a git project current branch and latest commit data.
Predicates for accessing a git project current branch and latest commit data.

Glicko-2 pairwise preference ranker. GLPK (GNU Linear Programming Kit) linear and mixed-integer programming backend using the ``glpsol`` command-line tool. Supports the ``executable/1``, ``time_limit/1`` (rounded up to whole seconds), and ``mip_gap/1`` options.

HiGHS linear and mixed-integer programming backend using the ``highs`` command-line tool. Supports the ``executable/1`` and ``time_limit/1`` options. The ``mip_gap/1`` option is not supported (the HiGHS command-line tool can only set it using an options file) and is rejected.
SCIP linear and mixed-integer programming backend using the ``scip`` command-line tool. Supports the ``executable/1``, ``time_limit/1``, and ``mip_gap/1`` (relative gap) options.
Portable dense two-phase simplex solver for small continuous linear programs.
Portable depth-first branch-and-bound solver for small mixed-integer linear programs.

Linear regression regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using a direct ordinary least-squares solve. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``regression_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a regressor term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.

Linear support vector machine classifier supporting binary and multiclass classification using one-vs-rest margin models. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a classifier term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.
Listing predicates.

Barzilai-Borwein (BB) gradient method with adaptive step sizes. Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``. Supports box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization, and BB1 / BB2 / alternating formulas.

BFGS (Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno) dense quasi-Newton local optimizer with backtracking Armijo line search. Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``. Supports optional box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization.

Nonlinear conjugate-gradient local optimizer (Fletcher-Reeves and Polak-Ribière). Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``. Supports optional box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization, and periodic or automatic restarts.

Gradient descent (steepest descent) local optimizer with optional backtracking Armijo line search. Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``. Supports box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization.

L-BFGS (limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno) quasi-Newton local optimizer with backtracking Armijo line search. Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2``. Supports optional box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization.

L-BFGS-B bound-constrained limited-memory quasi-Newton optimizer with a level-B approximate generalized Cauchy point (first-segment quadratic min along the projected gradient path), free-set identification at the Cauchy point, feasible-step limiting, and L-BFGS two-loop recursion. Requires ``gradient/2``.

Nelder-Mead (downhill simplex) derivative-free local optimizer for continuous problems. Supports optional box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization, and the standard reflection / expansion / contraction / shrink operators.

Trust-region Newton-CG local optimizer (Steihaug-CG for the subproblem). Requires the problem to define ``gradient/2`` and ``hessian/2``. Supports optional box constraints via projection, minimization and maximization.

Local Outlier Factor anomaly detector with multiple distance metrics, mixed-feature support, and missing-value handling. Learns from baseline training examples selected from a dataset object implementing the ``anomaly_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a detector term that can be used for scoring, prediction, and export.
Logging events to files protocol.
Logging events to files category.
Global logger object for logging events to files.

Logistic regression classifier supporting binary and multiclass classification using joint softmax training. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a classifier term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.
Loop control constructs protocol.
Loop control structures predicates.
LRU (Least Recently Used) cache protocol. Key-value pairs are represented as ``Key-Value``.
Immutable LRU (Least Recently Used) caches.

Massey pairwise preference ranker. Learns one deterministic rating per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by solving the Massey linear system built from aggregated pairwise outcomes and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Protocol for process-backed RC2, Open-WBO, and Z3 CLI weighted partial MaxSAT solving, WCNF source generation, and result inspection.
Protocol for ordered, ground weighted partial MaxSAT statement providers.
Canonical weighted partial MaxSAT statement validation, WCNF source generation, and variable table computation.
Whole-document RC2, Open-WBO, and Z3 plain-text MaxSAT output decoding.
Opt-in equivalent weighted partial MaxSAT directive and clause expansion for pure problem objects.
Isolated operating-system shell transport for the RC2, Open-WBO, and Z3 CLIs.
Process-backed RC2, Open-WBO, and Z3 CLI weighted partial MaxSAT solving, WCNF source generation, and collected result inspection.

Protocol for Logtalk objects that provide tools to be exposed via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Implementing objects must define the set of tools available and handle tool calls. Tool metadata (names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas) can be derived automatically from ``info/2`` and ``mode/2`` directives on the tool predicates, or overridden using ``input_schema/2`` and ``output_schema/2``. Used by both the 2025-06-18 and 2026-07-28 adapters.
Protocol for Logtalk objects that provide MCP prompt argument and resource URI completions. Used by the 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, and 2026-07-28 adapters.

Protocol for Logtalk objects that provide prompts to be exposed via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Implementing objects must define the set of prompts available and handle prompt get requests. Prompts are templates for structured LLM interactions that can accept arguments to customize their behavior. Used by both the 2025-06-18 and 2026-07-28 adapters.

Protocol for Logtalk objects that provide resources to be exposed via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Implementing objects must define the set of resources available and handle resource read requests. Applications may also expose parameterized resources using URI templates. Resources expose data and content from the application that MCP clients can access. Used by both the 2025-06-18 and 2026-07-28 adapters.

Protocol for multi-round tool/prompt/resource operations (MRTR) used by the MCP 2026-07-28 specification. Implementing objects may define the round hooks to request additional input from the client (elicitation, sampling, roots) and to resume with input responses and opaque request state. Existing applications that do not implement these hooks continue to use ``tool_call/3``, ``prompt_get/3``, ``resource_read/3``, or auto-dispatch; the 2026 adapter wraps those results as ``complete(Result)``. The 2026 adapter never invokes the 2025-06-18 ``tool_call/4`` elicitation API.

Optional protocol for per-operation cache policy used by the MCP 2026-07-28 specification. An application may implement ``cache_policy/4`` to choose TTL (milliseconds) and scope (``public`` or ``private``) for complete results of ``server/discover``, list operations (``tools/list``, ``prompts/list``, ``resources/list``, ``resources/templates/list``), and ``resources/read``. Cache fields are never attached to ``input_required`` results or MRTR retries. When the predicate is not defined, or for an operation it does not cover, the server falls back to the options ``cache_ttl(0)`` and ``cache_scope(private)``.

Optional MCP Apps (``io.modelcontextprotocol/ui``) metadata for tools and resources. Applications that provide interactive UI resources declare ``ui`` in ``capabilities/1`` (and typically ``resources``), implement ``mcp_resource_protocol`` for ``ui://`` HTML resources, and may implement these predicates to attach tool and resource UI metadata. See the https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/apps/overview spec for details.
Protocol for MCP server transports. The ``mcp_server`` facade object selects the transport via the ``transport/1`` option and delegates the server lifecycle to it.

Protocol for MCP server spec (aka data layer) handlers independent of transport. A handler validates and dispatches JSON-RPC messages and returns abstract outcomes that a transport (stdio or Streamable HTTP) renders to the wire.

Common predicates for MCP servers: tool/prompt/resource descriptor conversion, completion request handling, schema derivation from ``info/2`` and ``mode/2`` directives, auto-dispatch, canonical complete-result terms, curly-term predicates, and MCP Apps (``_meta.ui``) metadata.

MCP 2025-06-18 protocol handler. Transport-agnostic message handling; returns abstract outcomes for stdio or Streamable HTTP transports to render. Synchronous elicitation requires ``stdio_input/1`` and ``stdio_output/1`` options.

MCP 2025-11-25 protocol handler. Extends the 2025-06-18 handler with version ``2025-11-25`` negotiation (still accepting ``2025-06-18``), optional ``serverInfo.description``, icons metadata on tools/prompts/resources (SEP-973), and URL-mode elicitation (SEP-1036). EnumSchema / ElicitResult enrichments (SEP-1330) are pass-through via application-supplied schemas. Does **not** implement sampling tool calling, experimental Tasks, or OAuth/OIDC.
MCP 2026-07-28 protocol handler. Returns reply/1, reply_with_progress/2, subscribe/3, accepted, or no_reply outcomes. Does not write to streams; transports render outcomes.

Implements the stdio transport for MCP servers. Reads newline-delimited JSON-RPC from the input stream and writes responses to the output stream. Supports specs 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, and 2026-07-28 selected via the ``spec/1`` option and delegated to ``mcp_server_2025_06_18_spec``, ``mcp_server_2025_11_25_spec``, or ``mcp_server_2026_07_28_spec``.
MCP server facade. Selects spec and transport (stdio or Streamable HTTP).

Implements the Streamable HTTP transport for MCP servers. Uses Logtalk ``http_server::serve_until_shutdown/5`` and a dedicated ``http_handler_protocol`` handler object. Supports specs 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, and 2026-07-28 selected via the ``spec/1`` option and delegated to the matching ``mcp_server_*_spec`` object. Supports optional OAuth protection and protected-resource metadata publication using the ``oauth/4`` option. Long-lived subscriptions/listen streams emit periodic SSE comment keep-alives (``http_sse_keepalive/1``). Requires a multi-threaded backend for subscriptions/listen.
HTTP handler bridging http_server to mcp_server_streamable_http_transport. Uses http_core response/5 with json(Term) bodies for application/json.
Portable Memcached client implementing the text (ASCII) protocol. Uses the sockets library for TCP communication.
MessagePack format exporter and importer.
Useful meta-predicates protocol.
Some useful meta-predicates.
Compiler for the ``meta`` object meta-predicates. Generates auxiliary predicates in order to avoid meta-call overheads.
MIME type registry and convenience predicates for mapping file names and URLs to media types.
Protocol for process-backed MiniZinc solving, source generation, and result inspection.
Protocol for ordered, ground MiniZinc statement providers.
Canonical MiniZinc statement validation and source generation.
Decoding of the MiniZinc ``--json-stream`` message sequence into a collected result.
Opt-in directive expansion translating MiniZinc declaration directives into canonical statements for pure problem objects.
Isolated operating-system shell transport for the MiniZinc CLI.
Process-backed MiniZinc CLI solving, source generation, and collected result inspection.
Multi-layer perceptron classifier with configurable hidden layers and activation function, softmax output, and backpropagation training.

Statistical modified Z-score anomaly detector for continuous datasets. Learns per-attribute sample median and median absolute deviation from baseline training examples selected from a dataset object implementing the ``anomaly_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a detector term that can be used for scoring, prediction, and export.
Portable MQTT 5 client predicates using ``http_transport_protocol`` implementations.

Minimum redundancy maximum relevance selection using raw mutual information in bits and the MID difference criterion. Learning requires at least two joint complete observations; otherwise it throws ``domain_error(mrmr_usable_examples,Count)``.
Protocol for multiset operations over lists.
Implementation of multiset operations with repetition over lists.

Multivariate probability distributions using an injected random source.

Stores mutation definitions for selected types. User extensible by defining objects or categories defining clauses for the ``mutation/3`` predicate and using this object as a hook object for their compilation.
Adds mutations support to the library ``type`` object.

Selects categorical or discretized continuous features using mutual information or symmetrical uncertainty.

Naive Bayes classifier with Laplace smoothing and Gaussian distribution support. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a classifier term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.
NanoID generator protocol.
NanoID generator.
NanoID generator using atom representation, 21 symbols, and the standard URL alphabet.

Nearest Centroid classifier with multiple distance metrics. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a classifier term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.

One-class support vector machine anomaly detector with linear, polynomial, and radial basis function kernels. Learns from baseline training examples selected from a dataset object implementing the ``anomaly_dataset_protocol`` protocol.
Protocol for Logtalk objects that provide metadata used to derive OpenAPI 3.1.0 documents.
OpenAPI 3.1.0 document derivation, parsing, generation, and validation built on top of the ``json`` and ``json_schema`` libraries.

OpenSSL-backed JWT signature verification helpers.

OPTICS clusterer for continuous datasets. Learns an ordering from a dataset object implementing the ``clustering_dataset_protocol`` protocol and extracts clusters using an epsilon threshold so the result can be used with the standard clusterer protocol.

Constructors for optional terms. An optional term is either empty or holds a value. Optional terms should be regarded as opaque terms and always used with the ``optional/1`` object by passing the optional term as a parameter.
Optional term handling predicates. Requires passing an optional term (constructed using the ``optional`` object predicates) as a parameter.

Protocol for HOTP and TOTP generation and verification as specified in RFC 4226 and RFC 6238.
HOTP and TOTP generation and verification predicates.

Protocol for continuous bounded particle swarm optimization problem definitions. A problem object must define the three required predicates and may optionally define predicates for initial velocities, stopping, and progress reporting.

Continuous bounded global-best particle swarm optimization algorithm. Parameterized by a problem object implementing the ``particle_swarm_optimization_protocol`` protocol and by a random number generator algorithm for the ``fast_random`` library. The algorithm minimizes or maximizes the fitness function defined by the problem.
Particle swarm optimization algorithm using the Xoshiro128++ random number generator via ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)``.

Tie-aware Plackett-Luce grouped-ranking ranker. Learns one positive preference strength parameter per item from a dataset object implementing the ``ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by fitting a top-choice Plackett-Luce model to grouped tie blocks, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Shared connectivity, positive-strength, and iterative-update helpers for grouped ranking models that learn one strength parameter per item.
Shared helpers for grouped Plackett-Luce rankers.

Tie-aware Plackett-Luce-last grouped-ranking ranker. Learns one positive preference strength parameter per item from a dataset object implementing the ``ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by fitting a last-choice Plackett-Luce model to grouped tie blocks, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.

Queue protocol.
Queue predicates implemented using difference lists.
Random number generator protocol. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
Pseudo-random number generator protocol for seed handling predicates. These predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
Predicates for sampling probability distributions.
Portable random number generator predicates.
Portable random number generator predicates. Core predicates originally written by Richard O'Keefe. Based on algorithm AS 183 from Applied Statistics.
Random number generator predicates using the backend Prolog compiler built-in random generator.
Fast portable random number generator predicates.
Portable random number generator predicates. Core predicates originally written by Richard O'Keefe. Based on algorithm AS 183 from Applied Statistics.

Random Forest classifier using C4.5 decision trees as base learners. Builds an ensemble of decision trees trained on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets and combines their predictions through majority voting.
Random Forest regression using regression trees as base learners trained on bootstrap samples and per-split random feature subsets.
Random projection reducer for continuous datasets using a portable seeded Rademacher projection matrix.

Rank Centrality pairwise preference ranker. Learns one stationary probability score per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by applying power iteration to the Rank Centrality Markov chain built from aggregated head-to-head outcomes, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.

Ranked Pairs pairwise preference ranker. Learns one deterministic score per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by locking direct pairwise victories in descending strength order while avoiding cycles and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Protocol for machine learning rankers.
Shared predicates for ranker score access, diagnostics, and export.
Protocol for grouped ranking datasets.
Protocol for pairwise ranking datasets.
Protocol for pairwise measurement datasets.
Protocol for temporal pairwise ranking datasets with explicit rating periods and per-game outcomes.
Protocol for ordered multiplayer ranking datasets with ranked teams and weighted player participation.
Predicates for reading text file and text stream contents to lists of terms, characters, or character codes and for reading binary file and binary stream contents to lists of bytes.
Protocol for datasets used with collaborative filtering recommendation algorithms.
Protocol for item catalogs with feature occurrences or preweighted sparse content vectors.
Protocol for pluggable similarity metrics between two sparse vectors, used to compare two users (by their item ratings) or two items (by the ratings they received).
Shared helper predicates for sparse-vector overlap, numeric scaling, normalization, and correlation, reused by the library similarity metric objects.

Cosine similarity between two sparse Key-Value vectors, using scaled unit normalization to avoid squaring original magnitudes. Norms use each whole vector and the dot product uses common keys, treating missing entries as zeros. Results range from -1.0 to 1.0, or 0.0 to 1.0 for non-negative values. No common key or an all-zero vector gives 0.0.

Pearson correlation between two sparse Key-Value vectors, computed only over common keys using shifted, scaled centering and unit normalization. Results range from -1.0 to 1.0. Fewer than two common keys, or exactly constant values in either common-key subset, gives 0.0.

Jaccard similarity of the observed key sets of two sparse vectors: intersection size divided by union size. Values, including zeros, are ignored. Each key must occur at most once per vector. Results range from 0.0 to 1.0; an empty union gives 0.0.

Inverse mean-squared-difference similarity over common keys: 1 / (1 + MSD). Results range from 0.0 to 1.0, with 1.0 for identical common ratings and 0.0 when no keys are common. Scaled differences avoid squaring original magnitudes. Each key must occur at most once per vector.

Spearman rank correlation over common keys, using average ranks for numeric ties. Results range from -1.0 to 1.0. Fewer than two common keys or constant common values in either vector gives 0.0. Each key must occur at most once per vector.
Protocol for recommendation models and user-item relevance scoring.
Legacy recorded database predicates. Can be imported into an object to provide a local database.
Legacy recorded database predicates. Provides an application global database.
Redis client library with support for strings, keys, hashes, lists, sets, and sorted sets. Inspired by Sean Charles GNU Prolog Redis client.
Protocol for machine learning regressors.
Regression tree regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using recursive variance-reduction splits.

Regularized Bradley-Terry MAP ranker. Learns one positive strength parameter per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol using a Bradley-Terry likelihood with an explicit independent Gamma prior, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Binary Relief feature selection with one nearest hit and miss.
Multiclass ReliefF feature selection with class-prior miss weighting.

Ridge regression regressor supporting continuous and mixed-feature datasets using a direct weighted linear-system solve with L2 regularization. Process-backed Kissat, CaDiCaL, Glucose, and Z3 CLI solving, DIMACS CNF source generation, and collected result inspection.

Schulze pairwise preference ranker. Statistical calculations over a list of numbers.

Stemmer protocol for reducing words to their stems.

Lovins stemmer algorithm implementation for English words.
Stop-word language provider protocol.

Stop-word enumeration and filtering for a text representation and language provider.
Portable STOMP 1.2 (Simple Text Orientated Messaging Protocol) client. Uses the sockets library for TCP communication.
String distance predicates.

Protocol for subsequence operations over lists.
Implementation of subsequence operations over lists.

Support vector regression (SVR) using an epsilon-insensitive dual margin model with linear, polynomial, and radial basis function kernels, trained with a Pegasos-style dual subgradient descent loop. Learns from a dataset object implementing the ``regression_dataset_protocol`` protocol and returns a regressor term that can be used for prediction and exported as predicate clauses.
Protocol for tabu search problems, with optional tabu keys, tenure, aspiration, restart diversification, delta-energy generation, neighborhood enumeration, stopping, and progress reporting.

Tabu search optimization algorithm. Parameterized by a problem object implementing the ``tabu_search_problem_protocol`` protocol and by a random number generator algorithm for the ``fast_random`` library. Minimizes energy with optional problem-defined tabu keys, tenure, aspiration, restart states, neighbor generation, stopping, and progress reporting.
Tabu search optimization algorithm using the Xoshiro128++ random number generator via ``fast_random(xoshiro128pp)``.
Predicates for term input/output from/to atom, chars, and codes. The predicates are declared as synchronized when the library is compiled using a backend supporting threads.
Term input/output from/to atom, chars, and codes.
Text normalization protocol for text represented as atoms, lists of characters, or lists of character codes.
Profile provider protocol for extending text normalization policy without replacing Unicode normalization algorithms.
Optional provider protocol for spelling correction composed after text normalization.
Portable Unicode 17.0 normalization over lists of Unicode scalar values.
Portable Unicode 17.0 default case conversion over lists of Unicode scalar values.
Unicode diacritic removal and profile-defined transliteration over code lists.
Portable character reference decoding rules over lists of Unicode code points.
Portable Unicode whitespace, line-ending, and control-character normalization rules over code lists.
Text normalizer parameterized by text representation and normalization profile.
Protocol for learning and applying text vectorization models.
Binary, count, term-frequency, and TF-IDF sparse text vectorization.
Content-based recommender using TF-IDF item vectors, positive-feedback centroid profiles, and cosine relevance scores.
Standard Theta forecasting combining simple exponential smoothing and linear trend extrapolation.

Thurstone-Mosteller Case V pairwise preference ranker. Learns one real-valued latent utility per item from a dataset object implementing the ``pairwise_ranking_dataset_protocol`` protocol by fitting continuity-corrected empirical paired-comparison probabilities with a deterministic weighted least-squares normal model, and returns a self-describing ranker term with diagnostics that can be used for ranking and export.
Time scales conversion protocol for UTC, TAI, TT, UT1, TDB, GPS, GST, TCG, and TCB.
Bundled and override data plus constants for UTC/TAI/TT/UT1/TDB/TCG/TCB conversions.
Time scale conversions for UTC, TAI, TT, UT1, TDB, GPS, GST, TCG, and TCB using bundled and optional override data.
Protocol for datasets used with time series forecasting algorithms.
Protocol for time series forecasting models.

Autoregressive (AR) time series forecaster fitted by least squares, with optional intercept, optional differencing (ARI models), automatic order selection using information criteria, and support for missing observations represented as unbound variables.
Predicates for calling goal with a time limit.
Protocol for parsing Two-Line Element sets and performing approximate portable orbit propagation with near-earth and deep-space variants plus ground-track sampling.

Parser for Two-Line Element sets with an approximate portable propagator featuring automatic branching between near-earth and deep-space variants, a legacy two-body fallback model, and ground-track sampling.

Sentence splitting protocol for text represented as atoms, lists of characters, or lists of character codes.

Tokenizer and sentence splitter parameterized by text representation and language provider.

Reusable portable rules for tokenization and sentence splitting. Importing objects supply language-specific abbreviation and word punctuation hooks. URL and email address recognition delegates to the ``url`` library.
TOML parser and generator protocol.
TOML parser and generator.
TOML parser and generator. Uses compound terms for parsed TOML tables and dashes for parsed TOML pairs.
TOML parser and generator. Uses compound terms for parsed TOML tables, dashes for parsed TOML pairs, and atoms for parsed TOML string values.

TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) parser and generator. TOON is a compact, human-readable, line-oriented format that encodes the JSON data model.

TOON parser and generator. Uses curly terms for parsed TOON objects, dashes for parsed TOON pairs, and atoms for parsed TOON strings.
Persistent trie predicates supporting different string representations.

Constructors for validation terms. A validation term is either ``valid(Value)`` or ``invalid(Errors)`` where ``Errors`` is a list of errors. Validation terms allow applicative-style error accumulation.
Validation term predicates. Requires passing a validation term (constructed using the ``validation`` object predicates) as a parameter.
Types and predicates for type-checking and handling lists of validation terms. Inspired by Scala Cats and Kotlin Arrow.

Canonical weighted model counting statement validation, DIMACS CNF source generation with weights using the Model Counting Competition format, and variable table computation.
Whole-document Ganak and SharpSAT-TD plain-text model counting output decoding using the Model Counting Competition output format.

Intended for small problems and as an oracle for testing; use an external counter for larger problems.
Opt-in equivalent weighted model counting directive and clause expansion for pure problem objects.
